title: rename-journal — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins note_txn::recover_pending_rename (src-tauri/src/note_txn.rs, main myne repository) — the §9.12 rename-journal crash-recovery state machine — as an fs-state conformance fixture. NOT a byte-output codec: the .rename-journal marker is content-free and POSIX readdir is unordered, so each case pins a directory SNAPSHOT (a name-sorted set of {name, content_hex}) before and after recovery. The marker's presence is the only durability signal — present → roll forward (every *.myn.tmp renamed to *.myn, marker cleared); absent → roll back (every *.myn.tmp deleted); committed *.myn untouched. A port materializes input_dir_files in a fresh directory, runs its recovery, and asserts the resulting set equals expected_dir_files. case_kind labels the scenario (roll_forward / roll_back / noop). Recovery is idempotent (re-running is a fixed point). std/fs-bound category (like backup-container); runner is tests-side in note_txn.rs.

case_kind.description: roll_forward: marker present, staged .tmp committed. roll_back: no marker, staged .tmp discarded. noop: clean dir, unchanged.

input_dir_files.description: The directory snapshot before recovery (name-sorted set).

name.description: The file name within the notes directory. '.rename-journal' is the (empty) marker; '*.myn.tmp' are staged blobs; '*.myn' are committed blobs.

content_hex.description: The file's exact bytes (hex). Empty for the marker.

expected_dir_files.description: The directory snapshot after recovery (name-sorted set).
